newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady, except weak gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady, except weak gasoline.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly steady on Thursday, except gasoline which fell sharply, dealers said.
Naphtha prices were steady with traders awaiting the results of the Egyptian tender for 1997 expected in the next few days.
Traders said the market was well balanced with a Skikda cargo was sold at cif high plus $1.50 cif NWE.
"Most material is committed for and end users are satisfied for November," said one.
Gasoline fell with premium unleaded cargoes off $4 at $228/$230 cif.
Demand for most grades, including leaded and catgas, was weak, a refiner said.
Leaded was valued at cif high +$1 cif Italy while Spanish catgas loading on Nov 13-15 was bid as low as leaded fob Med quotes -$35 fob, he said.
Nigeria, a traditional buyer of this grade, was satisfying its own demand, he said.
Gas oil prices were steady. High sulphur demand was strong in Turkey, Greece, Egypt and east of Suez, but EU diesel was under pressure from an oversupply of Algerian cargoes, dealers said.
Turkey's 100,000 tonne buy tender for the second half of November is due to be awarded on Friday evening, and brings this country's imports to 225,000 tonnes for the month as a whole.
High sulphur cracked fuel oil was steady. Good demand for bunker quality material was balanced against sufficient avails.

"There's two cargoes needed into Gibralter and one into Italy, but we have a 50,000 tonne cargo loading in Syria and a couple of cargoes available in the second half," said one trader. Physical cargoes were pegged around $105.
Low sulphur edged higher late. Prices were put closer to $130 delivered. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8145
